description:
FOUND s491a (Opus) while building the #1917 guard.  PRE-EXISTING on main
337f6a23 and unrelated to #1917's subject: it fires for ANY die during the
load of a module PCL loads from its TEXT.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 prints nothing on stderr; PCL prints two extra lines):

  mkdir -p /tmp/d1917
  printf 'package Boom;\ndie "boom\\n";\n1;\n'          > /tmp/d1917/Boom.pm
  printf 'my $ok = eval { require Boom; 1 };\nprint "ok=", ($ok?1:0), "\\n";\n' > /tmp/d1917/p.pl
  perl   -I /tmp/d1917 /tmp/d1917/p.pl     # stdout "ok=0", stderr EMPTY
  ./pcl  -I /tmp/d1917 /tmp/d1917/p.pl     # stdout "ok=0", stderr:
  #   While evaluating the form starting at line 40, column 0
  #     of #P"/home/bernt/.pcl-cache/modules/XXXX.lisp":

MECHANISM: SBCL's LOAD of a SOURCE file (sb-impl::load-as-source) establishes a
handler-bind for `error` that PRINTS this context to *error-output* and then
DECLINES, so it prints whether or not an outer handler catches the condition.
PCL reaches that path in %p-load-module-cached-1's step-3 fallback and in
%p-load-module-uncached (./runpcl, --no-cache, the whole perl-tests sweep).
It does NOT fire for a module loaded from a FASL, which is why an :installed
module (site_perl) is quiet and a module under -I / PERL5LIB / `.` is not:
%p-compile-module-p answers the trust class, and :local means TEXT.

WHY IT MATTERS: it is stderr a perl program never writes, on a path a user
reaches by having their own lib/ -- and it defeats the one-line contract
#1247 (b) gave an uncaught perl die.  In Pl/t/require-xs-01.t's last row the
assertion had to be phrased as "says perl's message ONCE" rather than "stderr
is one line" because of it.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): the note cannot be muffled from outside -- SBCL's
handler is established INSIDE load and runs before any handler of ours.  The
options are (a) always compile to a fasl before loading (changes the trust-class
policy #1841/#1261 deliberately set), (b) load the text through our own reader
loop instead of LOAD (loses *load-pathname* and SBCL's own error contexts), or
(c) bind *error-output* to a filter around the load that drops exactly that
two-line form (a filter on a stream the module itself may legitimately write
to -- measure what a module's own warn does first).  Each has a cost; measure
before choosing.
subject: A die raised while loading a module under -I / lib prints SBCL's own "While evaluating the form starting at line N, column 0 of #P..." context note on stderr -- even when an eval catches it, and even though the die itself is a perl die with perl's one-line contract (#1247 (b))
